name: Palacio de los Duques, a Gran Meliá Hotel
insider_take: This isn't just a hotel—it's a palatial journey through Spanish aristocracy, where 19th-century grandeur meets contemporary luxury in the heart of Madrid's cultural triangle.
whats_special: Built as the Duke of Granada's private palace in 1850, this architectural masterpiece features original frescoed ceilings, marble columns, and a stunning glass-domed atrium. The hotel's prime location on Plaza de las Cortes places you steps from the Prado Museum and just minutes from the Royal Palace—making it Madrid's most culturally connected luxury property.
pro_tip: Book the Duke Suite for exclusive access to the original palace chambers with 20-foot ceilings and historical artifacts, plus complimentary private tours of the nearby Prado Museum can be arranged through the concierge.
dont_miss: The hotel's rooftop terrace offers panoramic views of Madrid's skyline, while the Dos Cielos restaurant (helmed by Michelin-starred chefs) serves avant-garde cuisine in the former ballroom. Take advantage of the hotel's "Art Triangle Package" for skip-the-line access to Prado, Reina Sofia, and Thyssen museums.
pros: Historic palace architecture with modern luxury amenities
Prime location in Madrid's cultural district near Royal Palace
Exceptional rooftop terrace with panoramic city views
Award-winning Montmartre restaurant with innovative cuisine
cons: Historic building constraints may limit room sizes in some categories
